study type: Convergent mixed methods study (quantitative retrospective comparison, qualitative analysis)
exposure: J9 Plus maternal-child accompaniment program (group antenatal care, group pediatric care, psychosocial support, community-based care)
outcome: Use of post-partum family planning methods
Incidence of pre-eclampsia with severe features
Patient perspectives of J9 care (ease of access, social support, maternal empowerment)
cohort: The study included maternal-newborn dyads born in 2019 at Hopital Universitaire de Mirebalais, comparing those receiving J9 care (n=524) to those receiving usual care (n=523).
finding: The J9 Plus maternal-child accompaniment model of care was associated with increased engagement in antenatal and postpartum care, increased utilization of post-partum family planning, and lower incidence of pre-eclampsia with severe features compared to usual care.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was higher in the J9 group (20%) compared to the usual care group (16%).
birth_weight: Low birth weight (did not differ across groups)
